messages:
alex: Heads-up — nightly perf dashboard flagged a sharp p95 latency increase on the v2 serving path starting around last merge. p50 moved ~18% and p95 ~60% on the long-tail models.

maria: ugh. any obvious signal from kernel selector or batching metrics?

perf-bot: alert: nightly/2026-11-02 04:00UTC — p95_latency_v2 +60% vs baseline; kv_eviction_rate +3x; batch_window_median decreased by 40ms.

alex: I pulled the perf traces. Looks like a routing change in the kernel selector that prefers small-batch fast kernels even when KV cache hit rate is low -> higher repeated kernel switch overhead. suspect commit c4f2a9b (runtime/kernel-routing): changed score function.

sam: CI perf job also had a failure on that commit — fyi. ci-bot, can you link?

ci-bot: perf-ci: job 7842 on commit c4f2a9b — benchmark suite 'nightly-throughput' showed 12% throughput regression and p95 latency increase. Full logs: https://ci.redwood/local/7842/logs

maria: if the selector is favoring small-kernels, that could explain KV churn. evictions spike when we miss on prefix caches and then switch kernels mid-sequence.

alex: I ran a quick local bisect script to confirm. steps:
```
git checkout main
git bisect start --good HEAD~10 --bad HEAD
# run microbench with profile
./scripts/run_perf_bench --model zeta-3 --trace kernel-routing
```

alex: bisect narrowed it to c4f2a9b -> behavior change in score function math. The new scoring added a penalty proportional to estimated KV hit, but the estimator is stale on warmup paths.

jen: rollout is currently blocked on this? product asked to hold canary earlier today.

alex: yes, I flagged the canary. best short-term fix is revert or force the old selector behavior via a config flag. I can prepare a revert PR or a hotfix toggle.

maria: prefer a toggle to avoid churn. we should also add a regression test that emulates low-kv-hit warmups and measures kernel-switch overhead.

sam: agree. I can update rollout policy to pause any further v2 capacity expansion until we have the toggle in.

jen: sounds good — if you have a toggle PR ready, we can ship ASAP. also add a trace id in the logs for better postmortem.

alex: creating PR now: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4512 — includes config flag `kernel_selector.use_old_score` and a perf test. cc @maria for test asserts.

maria: reviewing. will add the warmup-case to nightly perf suite so this doesn't regress silently.

perf-bot: note: when toggle is on, expected: p95 latency back within 5% of baseline.

ci-bot: queued: perf-ci run for PR 4512. results will post here when ready.

alex: thanks all — I'll hold canary and monitor next nightdash. if CI looks good we flip toggle in canary and then lift the block.

sam: i'll update ops runbook to include this debugging checklist (kernel score, kv eviction, batch_window).

jen: thanks team. keep updates short in this thread and ping if canary needs rollback. :thumbsup:
__notes: This document is a synthetic Slack thread for performance regression triage.
